title: A finite decreasing sequence admits a convex minorant with contact vertices
statement:
Work over the real field $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $n\geq1$ be an integer and let $w_0\geq w_1\geq\cdots\geq w_n$ be real numbers. There exist an integer $h\geq1$ and indices $0=a_0<a_1<\cdots<a_h=n$ with the following properties. For each integer $0\leq i\leq n$, define $v_i$ by affine interpolation between the successive selected vertices: if $a_j\leq i\leq a_{j+1}$, put
$$v_i=\frac{(a_{j+1}-i)w_{a_j}+(i-a_j)w_{a_{j+1}}}{a_{j+1}-a_j}.$$
The two formulas at a shared endpoint agree. Then $v_{a_j}=w_{a_j}$ for every $j$, $v_i\leq w_i$ for every $i$, and
$$v_{i+1}-v_i\leq v_{i+2}-v_{i+1}\qquad(0\leq i\leq n-2).$$
For $n=1$ the last condition has no instances. These displayed inequalities are the meaning of a convex minorant here.

proof.text: For integers $0\leq p<q\leq n$ put $s(p,q)=(w_q-w_p)/(q-p)$. For fixed $p<n$, select $b(p)\in\{p+1,\ldots,n\}$ minimizing $s(p,q)$. This selection is elementary: start with $q=p+1$, scan the remaining indices, and replace the current choice whenever a strictly smaller value is encountered. Induction on the number scanned says that the retained value is no greater than every scanned value. Thus $s(p,b(p))\leq s(p,q)$ for every $p<q\leq n$; ties may be retained arbitrarily.

source.place: Section 2.4, proof of Lemma 6, printed p.11 and Figure 2: explicit finite lower-envelope construction by Q52; source read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Start with $a_0=0$ and, whenever $a_j<n$, put $a_{j+1}=b(a_j)$. Each step increases the integer index by at least one and keeps it at most $n$. After $j$ steps $a_j\geq j$ by induction. Consequently a first stopping index $h$ exists with $a_h=n$ and $1\leq h\leq n$: otherwise the rule would give $a_n\geq n$ and then a further index greater than $n$. This gives $0=a_0<\cdots<a_h=n$.

source.place: Section 2.4, proof of Lemma 6, printed p.11 and Figure 2: explicit finite lower-envelope construction by Q52; source read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For each consecutive pair $p=a_j<q=a_{j+1}$ and integer $p\leq i\leq q$, define $v_i=w_p+(i-p)s(p,q)$. Expanding this expression gives precisely the affine formula in the statement. At $i=p,q$ it gives $w_p,w_q$, so both formulas at a shared vertex agree. For $p<i\leq q$, the minimizing property gives $s(p,q)\leq s(p,i)$; multiplying by $i-p>0$ and adding $w_p$ gives $v_i\leq w_i$. At $i=p$ there is equality. These intervals cover all integer indices from $0$ to $n$, so $v$ is defined everywhere and all required contact equalities and minorant inequalities hold.

source.place: Section 2.4, proof of Lemma 6, printed p.11 and Figure 2: explicit finite lower-envelope construction by Q52; source read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
For three successive selected vertices $p<q<r$, minimality at $p$ gives $s(p,q)\leq s(p,r)$. The direct identity
$$s(p,r)=\frac{(q-p)s(p,q)+(r-q)s(q,r)}{r-p}$$
then gives $(r-p)s(p,q)\leq(q-p)s(p,q)+(r-q)s(q,r)$. Subtracting the first term on the right and dividing by $r-q>0$ yields $s(p,q)\leq s(q,r)$. Hence the slopes of successive selected segments are nondecreasing.

source.place: Section 2.4, proof of Lemma 6, printed p.11 and Figure 2: explicit finite lower-envelope construction by Q52; source read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For each $0\leq i<n$, choose the unique $j$ with $a_j\leq i<a_{j+1}$. The two integers $i,i+1$ belong to that segment including its endpoints, so subtraction of its formula gives $v_{i+1}-v_i=s(a_j,a_{j+1})$. As $i$ increases, this segment index never decreases. Step 4 therefore implies $v_{i+1}-v_i\leq v_{i+2}-v_{i+1}$ for $0\leq i\leq n-2$. If $n=1$, the construction selects $0,1$ and this range is empty. No normalization or sign assumption on the weights has been used; in particular the argument applies to the given decreasing sequence.

One commit touching only the item and the report; the statement is unchanged, zero new nodes, no repair or re-split note for this item. Source: Morrison arXiv:0810.2340, §2.4 Lemma 6, printed pp.11-12, Fig. 2. The local PDF is absent, so I read the arXiv PDF. Its proof uses the 'lower convex envelope E of all the points' without constructing it; the item states that finite envelope, and the agent-written proof constructs it. Step 1: minimum-slope choice by finite scan over the nonempty set {p+1..n}. Step 2: strictly increasing recursion bounded by n, a_j>=j, so it stops with 1<=h<=n. Step 3: expanding w_p+(i-p)s(p,q) gives the statement's affine formula, and endpoint agreement holds; for p<i<=q, s(p,q)<=s(p,i) times i-p gives v_i<=w_i. Step 4: the identity (r-p)s(p,r)=(q-p)s(p,q)+(r-q)s(q,r) holds and r<=n is in p's scan range, so s(p,q)<=s(q,r). Step 5: unit differences equal the segment slope, so they are nondecreasing. All five steps are genuinely elementary and uses/proof_deps are empty. The consumer lem-sfb-strict-codegree-polygon-gap uses exactly contact, minorant, convexity and the affine formula. My own exact-rational test of the greedy construction covered n=1..5, entries -2..2 (non-monotone too) and both tie rules: 39,050 cases, 0 failures. rg -L over the DAG found no duplicate or generalization. Mathlib searches cover three kinds, no match. No SGA, no out-of-route citations. The stmt_dep def-weil-field for ordered R is inherited and harmless. No fixes.
